title: set takes --discovered-from, and the promote refusal names the right command
findings_note: s357 relay 2026-10-18: `field_in_promote_source` says "set them with `add` or `set`", but `set` has no `--discovered-from`; only `add --discovered-from` sets it
boundary: **Not in this slice:** which fields promote applies.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: s357 made `promote` refuse `parent` and `discovered_from` in a source outline. The refusal tells the author to use `add` or `set`, but after an item exists nothing can set or clear `discovered_from`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`set` parser), `src/slicer/ops.py` (set path; the refusal message names each key's command).
- `tests/test_ops.py` or `tests/test_cli.py`; `docs/commands.md` (set row); `CHANGELOG.md` under Added.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Set_DiscoveredFrom_SetsAndClears` (`''` clears; an unknown id refuses like `--parent`).
- `test_Promote_SourceWithDiscoveredFrom_MessageNamesSet`

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; watch them go red.
2. Add `set --discovered-from ID` with the same validation as `add`; `''` clears.
3. Docs, CHANGELOG; mutation-check.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
